about: How `screenshot` shows a page: one screen at a time ([[REQ-363]]).
WHY TILES. A full-page shot reduced on its longest edge leaves a tall page a
sliver: a 1280x9059 desktop page arrived as 169x1024 in the Charlie's
Plumbing session, and nothing on it could be read. A visitor sees one screen
and scrolls, so a page picture is a screen-height tile, reduced by WIDTH.
- `default_tiles`: which tiles a call with no `tiles` and no `section` gets.
`1` is the screen a visitor sees on arrival. `3`, `2-5` and `all` are the
- `default_detail`: the detail a call that names none gets.
- `max_tiles_per_call`: the most tiles one call returns. Asking for more
returns the first batch and says what remains, never refuses.
- `detail_widths`: the widest a tile is sent at, per detail. A tile is never
upscaled, so a narrower viewport (mobile 375) is always sent as it is.
- `provider_max_edge`: the provider downscales any image with an edge over
this before the model sees it, so no tile is sent with an edge past it.
- `pixels_per_token`: the provider's image price, width x height / this, used
only to state each tile's approximate cost in its label.
Changing any of these changes `screenshot` with no code change.
